latest.content:

Requisitioned General Meeting
Posting of Circular
Notice of Reconvened AGM
Union Jack Oil plc (AIM: UJO, OTCQB: UJOGF) announces that, following the receipt of a requisition notice dated 7 July 2026 (the "Notice") from shareholders (the "Requisitioners") holding 20,650,096 ordinary shares in the Company representing 14.09% of the total voting rights, the requisitioned general meeting ("Requisitioned GM" or "Requisition", as the context permits) will be held at 11:00 a.m. on 24 August 2026 at the offices of Keystone Law at 48 Chancery Lane, London WC2A 1JF.
The Company will today post a circular to shareholders (the "Circular") convening the Requisitioned GM and outlining the unanimous recommendation by the Company's board of directors ("Board") to vote
AGAINST
all of the resolutions to be proposed at the Requisitioned GM. The Board believes that the Requisition is misguided, ill-timed and destined to lead to a destruction in value for the Company's shareholders. The Board further believes that by proposing the Resolutions just six days after the announcement of the all share offer by Reabold Resources plc (the "Offer"), the Requisitioners are simply being opportunistic by seeking to replace the Board during the Offer process without providing the Company's shareholders with the opportunity to realise a control premium. A copy of the Circular will be available on the Company's website.
Reconvened AGM
Further to the announcement dated 7 July 2026, the Company will also reconvene the adjourned Annual General Meeting ("Reconvened AGM") at 12:00 p.m. on 24 August 2026
(
or as soon thereafter as the Requisitioned GM has concluded), also at the offices of Keystone Law at 48 Chancery Lane, London WC2A 1JF. The Reconvened AGM is a continuation of the Annual General Meeting ("AGM") convened pursuant to the notice of AGM dated 22 May 2026 (the "AGM Notice") which is set out on pages 81 and 82 of the Company's Annual Report for the year ended 31 December 2025. A copy of this announcement will be posted to shareholders today, together with the Circular.
The business to be transacted at the Reconvened AGM will be the same as that set out in the AGM Notice and no new resolutions will be proposed, except in the case of Resolutions 4 and 6 as Graham Bull and John Americanos have since ceased to hold office as directors of the Company. Accordingly, Resolutions 4 and 6, which proposed the re-election of Graham Bull and John Americanos as directors have become inapplicable and will not be put to the Reconvened AGM. Any proxy appointments or voting instructions received in respect of Resolutions 4 and 6 will not be counted. All other resolutions remain unchanged. A resolution proposing the appointment of John Americanos to the Board of the Company will be included in the resolutions put to shareholders at the Requisitioned GM.
Other than in respect of Resolution 4 and 6, proxy votes validly submitted in respect of the AGM will remain valid for the Reconvened AGM and will be counted unless they are validly revoked or amended.
Proxy forms are not automatically being reissued to shareholders in connection with the Reconvened AGM.
Shareholders who have already submitted a proxy form and who wish to change their voting instructions may do so by
contacting
Computershare
Investor Services PLC on 0370 702 0000 and a replacement form will be provided upon request.
Where a shareholder submits a new valid proxy appointment before the applicable deadline, the new appointment will supersede any earlier proxy appointment.
Shareholders who have not yet submitted a proxy appointment may do so by 12:00 p.m. on 20 August 2026, or, if applicable, by using the CREST proxy appointment service in accordance with the procedures described in the AGM Notice.
Copies of the Circular and AGM Notice will be available on the Company's website at:
https://unionjackoil.com
.

latest.title: Adjourned Annual General Meeting
latest.content:
Today 12:02
RNS Number : 3512L
Union Jack Oil PLC
07 July 2026
7 July 2026
Union Jack Oil plc
("Union Jack" or the "Company")
Adjourned Annual General Meeting
Union Jack Oil plc (the "Company") announces that, following the adjournment of its Annual General Meeting ("AGM")
originally convened on 26 June 2026 and following the announcement on 1 July 2026 by Reabold Resources plc ("Reabold") of a recommended all share offer to acquire all of the issued share capital of the Company (the "Offer"), the adjourned AGM will be held on the date falling five business days after the earlier of (i) 21 days after publication of the offer document containing the terms and conditions of the Offer (the "Offer Document") and (ii) the date on which the Offer becomes or is declared unconditional.
Accordingly, following publication of the Offer Document, a further announcement will be made notifying shareholders of the actual date of the adjourned AGM, together with details of the time and the venue of the meeting.
In further delaying the adjourned AGM, the Company recognises that it is denying shareholders the ability to vote against the re-election of the board of directors (the "Board") immediately, as proxy votes received by the Company for the adjourned AGM indicate that all members of the Board would have been removed from office had the AGM proceeded on 26 June,
assuming no change in voting intentions either at or before the meeting.
The Board considers the delay in reconvening the adjourned AGM is important in the face of determined opposition from two shareholders, Craig Howie and John Americanos, who the Board believes would attempt to frustrate the Offer process if they were appointed to the Board. These two individuals have confirmed that they are against any offer for the Company from Reabold.

company_30s.what_they_do: UJO is a small oil‑and‑gas exploration company that owns a handful of drill sites in Oklahoma.  Its main business is to develop these assets, hoping to bring the wells into production and eventually sell the company or its assets to a larger operator.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The U.S. shale market still offers high upside for companies that can get a well into production.  If UJO can prove its wells are commercially viable, it could become an attractive acquisition target for a larger player, or it could generate cash flow that would lift the share price.
company_30s.current_state: UJO is still in the exploration phase, with no revenue yet.  The company is burning cash to keep drilling and to pay for regulatory and operational costs.  It is currently trading well below its all‑time high, which has attracted a handful of contrarian traders.

rns_narrative: The company has been busy with corporate housekeeping – a director resigned, AGM resolutions were filed, and a rule‑2.9 disclosure was made.  These are routine, but they keep the company compliant and prevent a sudden collapse.

A second theme is a potential takeover.  Multiple RNS items mention a possible offer from Reabold Resources (RBD), a larger operator that already owns a stake in the same region.  If RBD steps in, the price could jump to a level that reflects the value of the asset portfolio.

The third thread is operational progress on the Crossroads Well.  The company has just completed a drilling update and is waiting for production data.  Positive results could validate the asset and attract buyers.

crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls are pointing to the RBD offer as a catalyst that could lift the price dramatically.  They see the company as a paper asset that could be bought at a discount.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the wells may never reach commercial viability and that the company will keep draining cash.  They also fear that the RBD offer could be a low‑ball, leaving shareholders with a paper loss.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter has moved from neutral to mildly bullish as the RBD offer rumor gained traction, but overall volume remains low.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for UJO is flat, indicating no public interest right now – a classic contrarian green‑light.

near_term_catalysts: An official takeover announcement from RBD – the most likely event to trigger a jump.
Positive drilling results from the Crossroads Well that show the well can produce at a commercial rate.
A financing round that injects cash, signalling the company can survive until production starts.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a volume spike of 2‑3× the average, a break above the 52‑week low, and any mention of a concrete offer or financing agreement in the news feed.
expect_next.timing_regime: UJO is in the early phase of a deep crash – the market has already capitulated.  The APEX score of 8 suggests the price is tightly compressed and ready for a breakout if a catalyst arrives.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The share is trading at roughly 14% of its all‑time high.  If a takeover or strong drilling data pushes the price to 50% of the ATH, the upside is about 4× the current level – a classic mean‑reversion play with asymmetric risk.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the wells fail to prove commercial viability or if the takeover offer falls through, the stock could stay near its current low or even drop further.  The worst‑case is a continued cash burn that forces the company to liquidate assets at a loss.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss: 14% of the ATH (the current price).  Potential gain: 36% of the ATH (halfway).  Risk‑to‑reward ratio roughly 1:3.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a breakout above the 52‑week low with a stop 1–2 pips below that level.  Allocate no more than 5% of the portfolio to this position, and trail the stop as the price climbs.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash or a small position until you see a volume spike of 2× the average or a clear announcement of a takeover or financing.  Then enter.
playbook.if_passing: None – no imminent delisting or bankruptcy signals have been identified.

ai_insights.bottom_line: UJO is a deep‑crashed, low‑volume play that could double in value if a takeover or positive drilling data surfaces – the upside outweighs the downside in a classic contrarian set‑up.
